name: GROWTH
description: GROWTH returns values along an exponential growth curve fitted by least squares to known data, predicting one or many y-values for the supplied x-values. It is an array function.
tldr: Fits an exponential curve and returns predicted y-values (array).

parameters.name: known_ys
parameters.description: The dependent (y) values of the known data used to fit the curve.

parameters.name: known_xs
parameters.description: The independent (x) values of the known data; defaults to 1,2,3,... if omitted.

parameters.name: new_xs
parameters.description: The x-values at which to predict y. If omitted, the known x-values are reused.

parameters.name: const
parameters.description: TRUE (or omitted) fits y = b*m^x; FALSE forces b = 1 (y = m^x).

basicExample.description: Predict a single future point on an exponential series
basicExample.explanation: The data follows y = 1*2^x, so at x=6 the prediction is 2^6 = 64.

advancedExamples.title: Predict several points at once
advancedExamples.description: Supply an array of new x-values to get an array of predictions
advancedExamples.explanation: Spills two values: 64 at x=6 and 128 at x=7. In older Excel confirm with Ctrl+Shift+Enter; in Microsoft 365 it spills automatically.

advancedExamples.title: Force base only (b = 1)
advancedExamples.result: Predicted y-values with b fixed to 1
advancedExamples.explanation: Fit becomes y = m^x, dropping the leading coefficient b.

howItWorks: GROWTH fits the model y = b*m^x by taking the natural logarithm of the known y-values and running a linear regression on ln(y), then exponentiating the result back. Because it accepts an array for new_xs, it can return many predictions at once. It is the exponential counterpart to the linear TREND.

howToSteps.name: Provide known data
howToSteps.text: List known y-values and, optionally, known x-values.

howToSteps.name: Provide new x-values
howToSteps.text: List the x-points you want to predict (a single cell or a range).

howToSteps.name: Enter as array
howToSteps.text: Type =GROWTH(known_ys, known_xs, new_xs) and press Enter (or Ctrl+Shift+Enter in legacy Excel).

limitations: Models only an exponential relationship; use TREND for linear patterns.
known_xs and known_ys must have the same number of points, or #REF! is returned.
Known y-values must be positive, since the fit takes their logarithm; zeros or negatives cause #NUM!.
Returns an array, so in pre-dynamic Excel it must be entered as an array formula.

commonErrors.cause: A known y-value is zero, negative, or blank, so its logarithm is undefined.
commonErrors.fix: Use only positive known y-values, or shift the data.

commonErrors.cause: known_xs and known_ys differ in size, or output cannot spill.
commonErrors.fix: Match the known array sizes and keep output cells empty.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: GROWTH works as an array function in Google Sheets, returning a row/column of predictions.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Identical behavior; results spill across cells in Sheets too.

faq.question: How is GROWTH different from TREND?
faq.answer: TREND fits a straight line; GROWTH fits an exponential curve y = b*m^x.

faq.question: Why does GROWTH need positive y-values?
faq.answer: It fits on the logarithm of y, and log(0) and log(negative) are undefined.

faq.question: Does GROWTH need array entry?
faq.answer: In Microsoft 365 it spills automatically; in older Excel use Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
